text: Soren Lindqvist and Dr. Amara Osei start translating Meridian's 'pick 4 of 12' problem into math a quantum algorithm can actually use.
Twelve binary variables, one per candidate asset -- x_i equals 1 means that asset gets selected.
The objective combines expected return with a risk-aversion-weighted covariance penalty.
A QUBO can't express 'exactly 4' directly, so the cardinality rule becomes its own penalty term inside the same objective.
Next: planning Felix Nakamura's classical baseline, and how to judge a QAOA result fairly.
